{"consolidated_memory":"FLAPPING FLAG EVALUATOR: Five separate incidents in platform/featureflags/eval.go (Go stack)

All incidents share the same symptom: a decision that alternates between calls when evaluating the same flag for one user repeatedly. All are covered by tests in platform/featureflags/eval_test.go.

OCCASION 1 [2026-01-10, c010-e0]:
Trigger: Sessions that arrived through the OAuth provider
Root cause: Off-by-one in the slice bound
Fix: Corrected the bound and added a property test around it (PR #1617, branch fix/flapping-flag-1)
Result: 7 duplicate rows a day stopped being written

OCCASION 2 [2026-01-26, c010-e1]:
Trigger: After the client had already retried once
Root cause: A listener registered but never removed
Fix: Removed the listener on teardown and asserted it in a test (PR #2352, branch fix/flapping-flag-2)
Result: The flaky test went from 9 failures per hundred runs to zero

OCCASION 3 [2026-02-25, c010-e3]:
Trigger: Deeply nested inputs beyond six levels
Root cause: An error swallowed by a bare except
Fix: Narrowed the handler and let the failure propagate (PR #6277, branch fix/flapping-flag-4)
Result: Throughput rose 24 percent, to 814 requests per second

OCCASION 4 [2026-06-04, c010-e5]:
Trigger: When the input list came in empty
Root cause: Missing Unicode normalisation before hashing
Fix: Normalised to NFC ahead of the digest (PR #8127, branch fix/flapping-flag-6)
Result: The alert stayed quiet for 56 consecutive days

OCCASION 5 [2026-08-31, c010-e7]:
Trigger: Jobs scheduled across the midnight boundary
Root cause: Clock skew between the two hosts
Fix: Switched the deadline to a monotonic clock (PR #9178, branch fix/flapping-flag-8)
Result: The error rate dropped from 2.7 percent to under 4 per ten thousand"}
